questions.stem: Under-5 mortality falls steadily from the poorest to the richest household quintile within a country. What does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Health improves step by step with socioeconomic position. A: A threshold would affect only the poorest. B: Not genetic. D: The pattern is systematic. E: Too narrow.
questions.source: The Social Determinants of Health, slide 11

questions.stem: The WHO defines social determinants of health as the conditions in which people are born, grow, live, work and age. What does the WHO say shapes these conditions?

options.C: Availability and quality of health care services
options.E: Distribution of money, power and resources

questions.explanation: The WHO definition states these conditions are shaped by the distribution of money, power and resources at global and local levels. A, B, D: Layers of the Dahlgren–Whitehead model, not what the WHO definition names as the shaping force. C: Health care services are one determinant among many.
questions.source: The Social Determinants of Health, slides 4–5

questions.stem: Road traffic deaths fell in highly motorized countries between 1987 and 1995 mainly because of:

options.A: Policies such as compulsory seat belts and drunk-driving penalties
options.D: Lower speed of vehicles due to congestion

questions.explanation: The lecture cites seat-belt laws and penalties for driving under the influence. B, C, D, E: Not the cited cause.
questions.source: The Social Determinants of Health, slide 20

questions.stem: According to the lecture, which sectors should health policy addressing the social determinants of health involve?

options.A: The health ministry alone, since health is its mandate
options.B: Health and finance ministries, which fund care
options.C: All sectors, since policy in each one shapes health
options.D: The private sector, through insurance coverage

questions.explanation: Policy relevance of SDH: health concerns should involve all sectors (transport, economy, employment, education, agriculture, environment, security), not just health policy. A, B, D, E: Too narrow; each leaves out sectors that shape health.
questions.source: The Social Determinants of Health, slide 6

questions.stem: Two unemployed men receive identical income support and housing. The one who feels ashamed of being jobless and is shunned by his neighbours has worse health. What does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Beyond material conditions, the social meaning of being poor, unemployed or excluded, including stigma, affects health. A: Their material circumstances are identical. C: The gradient compares socioeconomic levels; both men are at the same level. D: Access is not mentioned as different. E: Nothing suggests a genetic cause.
questions.source: The Social Determinants of Health, slides 11, 14
